why.text: A flat, sunny landscape with about 3000 sun hours a year and hot, dry summers, on varied soils from limestone to granite, with many native and recent grapes.

styles.text: Mostly still red, rosé and white wine; sparkling and fortified wines are made in smaller volumes.

climate.text: Temperate, Mediterranean and continental, with hot, dry springs and summers and rain mostly in winter. Rainfall is 550 to 650 mm a year (Borba 750 to 850, Portalegre 900 to 1000). Mean temperature is 15.5 to 16 °C, with about 3000 sun hours a year.

soil.text: Varies by sub-region: crystalline limestone in Borba, granite in Portalegre, eruptive rocks in Redondo and Reguengos, red and brown Mediterranean soils in Évora. Alluvial, colluvial, black clay and non-limestone brown-red clay soils are excluded.

altitude.text: Only Portalegre sets a limit: areas above 700 m are excluded.

tastes.text: Young wines are fruity and/or floral, gaining more complex tertiary aromas with age. Reds run from ruby to deep red, whites from pale lemon to slightly golden, rosés from pink to salmon.

styles.name: Espumante
styles.text: Sparkling wine made by classic bottle fermentation, minimum 11% alcohol.

styles.name: Licoroso
styles.text: Fortified: neutral wine alcohol or wine distillate added to fermenting must, minimum 17.5%.

styles.name: Reserva
styles.text: Quality term; needs standout structure and balance, tasting score of 66 or more.

styles.name: Garrafeira
styles.text: Quality term; needs standout structure and balance, tasting score of 66 or more.
